page: Amazon Web Services c8gn.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors running the 64-bit arm64 ARMv9 architecture. The instance provides 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz, coupled with 128.0 GB of system memory at a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Networking capabilities are anchored by a 200 Gbps baseline interface. The instance incorporates hardware AES acceleration, while omitting discrete graphics processors and onboard local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistence.

Performance benchmarks demonstrate exceptional parallel compute execution and memory subsystem throughput against moderate single-threaded performance. Multi-core results place in the highest percentiles, featuring strong results in Geekbench multi-core tests, clang compilation benchmarks, and PassMark database operations. The memory subsystem exhibits top-tier transfer rates, recording 466.64 GB/sec for large-block uncached read operations. Network-centric evaluation shows high throughput, reaching 116.84 GB/sec in static web serving tests and 144.9 million operations per second during Redis SET benchmarks, while single-core Geekbench and stress-ng scores reflect average middle-tier execution.

The primary tradeoff of the c8gn.16xlarge involves its specialized arm64 footprint and a modest 2.0 GB memory-to-core allocation, which may constrain memory-heavy single-node tasks. However, its high core density and 200 Gbps network pipe provide strong efficiency for horizontally scaling environments. The instance is suited for multi-threaded compilation pipelines, high-throughput in-memory caching tiers, static web delivery at scale, and high-concurrency microservices relying on networked block volumes.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gn.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by 64 dedicated AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 physical cores based on the ARMv9 architecture. Running at 2.8 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor, it features 128.0 GB of system memory and 200 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. The instance does not include local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage. Benchmark testing indicates top-tier multi-threaded processing, reflected in elevated Geekbench multi-core results, clang compile speed, and uncached memory read bandwidth of 466.64 GB/sec, contrasted with average single-core metrics. High network capacity facilitates strong Redis and static web serving throughput. With a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio, the instance is well suited for concurrent workloads including software build systems, network-bound caching, distributed database nodes, and containerized microservice backends.
